S68.01.needs: a second client signed in to the same account
S68.01.note: The Code line cites ChatStateManager.ts:340, which now holds the sendMessage type, not the identifier logic; the session identifier itself has no visible text.
steps: Click the Sessions icon in the sidebar header and note the session title on the Local tab.
Open the same session on the second client and compare the title and row shown with Expected.
S68.01.where: No control of its own. Its effect shows as the same session title and row in the Sessions sheet on each client

S68.02.needs: a second client (VS Code, CLI or desktop) signed in to the same account and the same workspace
steps: Click the Sessions icon (tooltip Sessions) in the sidebar header.
Make sure the Local tab is selected, then click a session row.
Compare the conversation history shown with the history on the second client, as Expected.
S68.02.where: Sessions icon in the sidebar header > Local tab > click a session row

S68.03.needs: a cloud session that has a working branch, and a second client on the same account
S68.03.note: The branch appears as small text on the row with no label of its own.
steps: Click the Sessions icon in the sidebar header.
Click the Cloud tab.
Read the branch text under a session row (shown only when the session has a working branch).
Compare the branch with the branch the same session shows on the second client.
S68.03.where: Sessions icon in the sidebar header > Cloud tab > look at the branch line under a session row

S68.04.needs: a folder with a GitHub git remote and a pushed branch
S68.04.note: The Cloud tab list is filtered to sessions of the repository open in the window, but no row shows the repository name directly.
steps: Open a folder whose git remote is on GitHub, with its branch pushed.
Open the Command Palette and run Code: Continue in the Cloud.
Type a goal and press Enter.
Read the Repository: line in the review dialog and compare it with the repository on the other client, then click Cancel.
S68.04.where: Command palette > Code: Continue in the Cloud > type a goal > review dialog line Repository:

labels.text: Code: New Session in a Worktree

S68.05.needs: a git repository with at least one session worktree
S68.05.note: The Code line cited sessionWorktrees.ts lines that moved; the command and its worktree list are present in the file.
steps: Open the Command Palette and run Code: Session Worktrees.
Read the list of worktrees and the branch named for each one.
Compare the worktree a session is tied to with the worktree shown on the second client.

S68.06.needs: a folder with a GitHub git remote and a pushed branch
S68.06.note: No screen was found that shows the instruction files a session uses.
steps: Run Code: Continue in the Cloud, type a goal and press Enter.
Read the Model: line in the review dialog and compare it with the model shown on the second client.
Click Cancel.
S68.06.where: No control of its own. Its visible effect is the Model: line in the Code: Continue in the Cloud review dialog

S68.07.needs: a session that already has at least one prompt
S68.07.note: No separate task-plan screen was found; the plan appears only in the chat. The Code line cited lines that moved.
steps: Open a chat with some turns in it.
Open the Command Palette and run Code: Checkpoints.
Read the checkpoints listed for the session, and the Checkpoints item in the chat menu if it shows.
Compare the checkpoints with those on the second client.

S68.08.needs: a cloud session with a pending approval, and a second client on the same account
S68.08.note: The approve item text is built from Approve plus ' and continue'.
steps: Click the Sessions icon in the sidebar header and click the Cloud tab.
Click a cloud session that is waiting for an approval.
Read the Approval required section at the top of the list (items show Approve and continue or Reject).
Answer it here, then check the second client shows the answer.
S68.08.where: Sessions icon in the sidebar header > Cloud tab > click a session row > Approval required

S68.09.needs: a cloud session that is running a turn, and a second client on the same account
S68.09.note: No separate view of tool activity was found in this app.
steps: Start a turn in a cloud session from one client.
Open the same session on the second client and watch the progress notice that reads Working while the turn runs.
S68.09.where: No control of its own. Its visible effect is tool lines appearing live in an open cloud session while a turn runs

S68.13.needs: a cloud session on the same account
steps: Click the Sessions icon in the sidebar header and click the Cloud tab.
Click a cloud session row.
In the list, click Continue here and confirm the review dialog.
Check the chat in this window now shows the session's conversation, and that the handoff is explicit.
S68.13.where: Sessions icon in the sidebar header > Cloud tab > click a session row > Continue here

S68.14.needs: a phone with the Mobile app signed in to the same account, a folder open in VS Code, a trusted workspace
S68.14.note: The phone-side wording is taken from the text in the desktop code; the phone app is outside this folder and was not checked.
steps: Sign in to AGI in VS Code and open a folder, trusting the workspace.
Run Code: Remote Control from the Command Palette and click Pair a phone.
On the phone, open the Mobile app, choose Pair with Desktop and scan the code.
On the phone, open a local session from this folder and send a message, then check it runs on this computer.
S68.14.where: Command palette > Code: Remote Control > Pair a phone; then on the phone, Pair with Desktop

S68.16.needs: a folder with a GitHub git remote and a pushed branch, and a signed-in AGI account
S68.16.note: Code line says unfinished: session creation needs AGI_E2B_EXECUTION on in production, so the cloud run may not start.
steps: Click the Sessions icon in the sidebar header and click the Cloud tab.
Click the Continue in the cloud icon (tooltip Continue in the cloud) in the sheet header.
Type a goal, read the review dialog, and click Continue in the cloud to start, or Cancel to stop.
Check the cloud session appears on the Cloud tab with the goal as its title.
S68.16.where: Sessions icon in the sidebar header > Cloud tab > Continue in the cloud icon in the sheet header

S68.17.needs: a cloud session with a working branch on a GitHub repository, and a local folder with that repository open
steps: Click the Sessions icon in the sidebar header and click the Cloud tab.
Click a cloud session that has a working branch.
Click Bring the branch in in the list.
If the folder has uncommitted files, read the list of files at stake and decide; then check the branch from the cloud session is checked out locally.
S68.17.where: Sessions icon in the sidebar header > Cloud tab > click a session row > Bring the branch in

labels.text: What moves: the task you typed and the pushed branch.
What stays here: this chat’s conversation, local tools and servers, and anything not pushed.

S68.18.needs: a folder with a GitHub git remote and a pushed branch
S68.18.note: The review dialog is the place the file and environment list is shown; no list of individual files is shown for a cloud move, only the uncommitted count.
steps: Open a folder with a GitHub remote and a pushed branch, with some uncommitted changes if you want to see that line.
Run Code: Continue in the Cloud and type a goal.
Read the review dialog: Repository, Branch, Model, Network, What moves and What stays here.
Click Cancel and check that nothing was started.
S68.18.where: Command palette > Code: Continue in the Cloud > type a goal > review dialog lines What moves and What stays here

S68.22.needs: a phone with the Mobile app signed in to the same account
steps: Sign in to AGI in VS Code.
Run Code: Remote Control from the Command Palette and click Pair a phone.
Read the Pairing code and the QR code shown on the panel.
On the phone, scan the code with Pair with Desktop, then check the panel shows Connected to, followed by the phone name.
S68.22.where: Command palette > Code: Remote Control > Pair a phone

S68.23.needs: a phone that is paired and connected
S68.23.note: The revoke-from-phone side is not in this folder; the desktop control is shown here.
steps: With a phone connected, run Code: Remote Control from the Command Palette.
Click Disconnect phone and read the Disconnect dialog.
Click Disconnect phone in the dialog.
On the phone, try to follow or steer a session and check it no longer connects.
S68.23.where: Command palette > Code: Remote Control > Disconnect phone (while connected); or Command Palette > Code: Stop Remote Control

S68.26.needs: a paired and connected phone, and a way to drop the network connection
S68.26.note: The reconnect step is in the remote control service; resuming the same chat state is in ChatStateManager, which has no separate screen.
steps: Pair and connect a phone with a session open.
Turn Wi-Fi off on the Mac for a few seconds, then back on.
Run Code: Remote Control and read the status: Connection lost, then Connected to the phone, and check the session on the phone shows the same history.
S68.26.where: No control of its own. Its visible effect is the Remote Control panel status changing to reconnecting and then back to connected

S68.30.needs: VS Code in the background and a session that can ask for approval
S68.30.note: Notices are posted only while the window is unfocused, and the cross-client source was not verified; the Code line cited sidebarProvider.ts and chatEditorPanel.ts lines that moved.
steps: Click another app so VS Code is not the focused window.
Start or wait for an approval in a session that is active in this window.
Watch for the notification Approval needed with the Open chat button.
Click Open chat and check the session shows the item waiting for approval.
S68.30.where: VS Code notification (shown when the VS Code window is not focused): Approval needed, with an Open chat button
